name: Raffles Seychelles
positioning: All-villa resort on Praslin Island, where every villa has a private pool and a private butler, set on hillsides and beachfront in a UNESCO area
best_for: Couples and families who want a private pool villa with butler service
Families wanting daily complimentary activities for toddlers, children and teenagers
Divers and nature lovers who want boat trips, dives and island excursions from the resort's beach

facts.text: It is an all-villa resort where every villa has a private pool, set on the hillsides of Praslin Island.
The resort sits in a UNESCO area with a tropical hillside and beachfront setting.
Villa guests are looked after by a private Raffles Butler.
The Two Bedroom Beachfront Pool Villa is a brief stroll from Anse Takamaka beach.
Private flights from Mahe reach the resort's own helipad in 15 minutes.
The fitness centre is equipped by TechnoGym, alongside a double infinity pool and long beach walks.
Complimentary activities for toddlers, children and teenagers run all day, every day.
Group or private sessions cover ashtanga, hatha, pranayama, prenatal and children's yoga, plus meditation.
The resort has had a total ban on single-use plastic since 2019.
The resort offers boat-based fun dives for certified divers, plus PADI Discover Scuba Diving experiences and courses.
Boat excursions leave directly from the resort's beach on Anse Takamaka.
The Sunset Escapade takes guests by car to Anse Lazio beach for chilled champagne and canapes served by their private butler.

highlights.text: Raffles Seychelles opened on Praslin in 2011 and was the first Raffles resort.
Giant Aldabra rescue tortoises live in the resort's grounds, and guests can meet and feed them.
The resort works with the Marine Conservation Society on a coral rehabilitation project, with a snorkelling trail to its coral nurseries.
Scenic helicopter flights leave from the resort's own private helipad.
Creole cooking classes are held in an open-air beach kitchen.

considerations.text: The resort's culinary and social spaces are being transformed, with work scheduled to continue until 15 October 2026 and alternative dining locations in place.
Most visitors fly into Seychelles International Airport on Mahe, then continue to Praslin by domestic flight, high-speed ferry, yacht or private helicopter.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing and a remote island location that requires connecting flights.
